subject: Service shift notice — regional cloud disruption and verification checklist
messages:
From: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
To: sarah.lin@acuitylabs.com
Cc: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 28 May 2029 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: Service shift notice — regional cloud disruption and verification checklist

Hi Sarah and Acuity team,

We wanted to notify you that a subset of our cloud provider's EU and APAC routing fabric experienced an outage starting ~08:50 UTC this morning that impacted incoming traffic termination into those regions for a span of time. The outage affected instance provisioning in eu-west and apac-south node pools and caused request failures or elevated 5xxs for some customers routing directly to those regions.

What we did (immediate actions):
- Automatically routed live traffic from EU/APAC ingress to our US fallbacks for requests to the Redwood inference API (this is the same routing policy we use for planned failovers).
- Switched affected customers to a compatible model variant (smaller quantized profile) where necessary to preserve throughput and reduce queueing.
- Bumped burst capacity for Dedicated pools to reduce throttling during the shift.

What we need from you (three quick asks):
1) Apply the attached traffic verification checklist so we can confirm you are reaching the US endpoints (steps 1–4). Attachment: reroute_instructions_v1.pdf
2) Share a short verification note once you see successful 200s for inference calls and acceptable latencies. If you see token-level errors or timeouts, include the request ids.
3) If you must maintain strict EU/APAC egress for compliance, reply immediately and we will open a priority ticket for an alternative plan.

Expected impact and timeline:
- The routing change is in effect now. Most customers will see an increase in median p50 latency of ~40–150ms depending on geography. We expect provider rollback or partial recovery within 6–12 hours, but we will keep you updated.

Credits & SLA: If you experienced sustained errors during the incident window, we will surface a credit review automatically. If you need an expedited SLA exception, reply with the scope and times.

Attachment: reroute_instructions_v1.pdf (PDF, 48KB) — step-by-step curl checks and endpoint hostnames.

I'll coordinate post-incident verification and follow up with a concise postmortem.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Karthik — forwarding quick internal status and a suggested follow-up email for customers who reported latency >500ms.

Summary:
- Provider reports control-plane degradation in eu-west that impacted new NAT allocations. Legacy connections that were already established remained fine, so the hit was mostly for burst provisioning and new sessions.
- We moved 1200 concurrent streams to US routing; autoscaler responded but some customers saw transient queuing.

Suggested edits for customer follow-ups: add a short snippet with steps to collect request ids, and include the traffic_verification_checklist.xlsx to speed confirmation. Also propose offering a 5% credit for customers with >30m continuous 5xx.

I updated the attachments and uploaded a live runbook link to the internal drive.

—Vanessa

Can you confirm:

From: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai

Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 29 May 2029 15:22:00 +0000
Subject: Post-incident update and verification checklist — Acuity Labs (EU/APAC outage)

Hi Sarah — thanks for the quick verification and the log snippet. Below is a concise post-incident summary and steps for final verification.

What happened (brief):
- The cloud provider experienced a control-plane regression impacting NAT allocation in eu-west and apac-south, which prevented creation of new egress paths for a subset of customer sessions. Established sessions were less affected.

Customer impact observed:
- Some requests returned 5xx during the 08:50–10:10 UTC window.
- Latency increased for customers routed to the US fallback; p95 increased by ~500–700ms for long-context use cases.

Why we routed to US and model variant details: 
- We prioritized continuous availability over regional latency; routing to US fallbacks preserves throughput and reduces error rates.
- Where capacity constraints occurred we temporarily served traffic with a compatible quantized model variant (same model family, lower-precision kernels). That can cause subtle output differences (tokenization and rounding effects), but it is functionally the same model architecture. We did not apply prompt or tokenizer changes.

Actions taken and remediation: 
- Provider confirmed rollback and partial remediation at 12:35 UTC; full restoration of eu-west/apac-south node pool capacity completed at 14:05 UTC.
- We validated successful reprovisioning and rolled traffic back to regional nodes at 14:10 UTC.
- We performed regression checks on a canonical prompt set for affected customers; for Acuity we saw one sample deviation consistent with quantization effects — we logged this under DEAL-ACUITY-2029Q2 for follow-up with R&D.

Your verification checklist (final steps):
1) Confirm you are receiving responses from the regional hostnames (see reroute_instructions_v1.pdf, step 4).
2) Run the provided QA prompt set; if you observe output drift, include request ids and the sample input.
3) If you want us to pin to the regional non-quantized flavor for the next 48 hours while we validate, reply and we will prioritize.

Next steps for us:
- We will prepare a short technical postmortem and a remediation timeline for long-term NAT allocation mitigation. Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/fake/postmortem-acuity-20290529 (attached as postmortem_summary_link.txt).
- We have queued a credit review for the incident window; you will see a notice in billing next week.
- R&D will triage the one reported model drift sample and report back within 72 hours.

Attachments included: traffic_verification_checklist.xlsx, postmortem_summary_link.txt

Please reply with confirmation once you run the final checks or if you need us to keep traffic pinned to US fallbacks for a short period.

Appreciate your patience — we know this was disruptive.

-Karthik
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
